title: Add Closed Hover Micro Animations to Every Icon
description: Add a hover-triggered micro animation to every icon in the UI. Trigger on hovering the icon itself or its enclosing interactive control (button, link, menu item, tab, etc.). Play once per hover-enter. Every animation must be closed: first keyframe equals last keyframe (rest -> motion -> identical rest), so it ends seamlessly and is loopable. Give every one of the 144 vendored Lucide icons (plus 10 more to be vendored: app-window, square-dashed, redo-2, undo-2, edit-3, align-left, list-ordered, text-cursor, clipboard, file) a bespoke, semantically fitting closed keyframe animation, keyed off the existing data-icon attribute on the central Icon component (ui/js/react/index.tsx). Also add data-icon-kind to non-catalog icon kinds (emoji, text, typst, url/data image, raw svg, node, missing-placeholder) with their own closed animations so literally every icon animates. Remap the non-Lucide "glb" icon id to the vendored "box" icon via an alias. Extend ui.css with the keyframes, a single generic hover-trigger rule, and a prefers-reduced-motion guard. Extend the in-source vitest tests in ui/js/react/index.tsx to assert completeness (every icon id has a keyframes block + assignment) and closed-ness (0% frame equals 100% frame, except declared full-turn spin exceptions ending at +/-360deg). Extend the Icons storybook story with a hover-animation demo grid.
summary:
Fourth refinement pass per user feedback: "The microanimations are violating physical properties. E.g. the hammer head is bending although a hammer is a rigid object. E.g. the trashbin lid is moving inside the bin instead of being lifted. All physical objects must behave correctly."

Root-caused and fixed two systematic bug classes across the icon animation system:

**A. Rotation-sign errors** (SVG viewBox is y-down, so `rotate(+deg)` is clockwise on screen — several hinges were authored with a y-up mental model). Verified mathematically before and after: trash-2's lid at the old `rotate(-32deg)` moved its free end `dy=+9.5px` (down, into the bin); flipped to `+32deg` now lifts it up (`dy=-9.5px`). Same bug fixed in lock's shackle (now pops open, not into the body) and lock-open's shackle (now swings further open instead of re-closing).

**B. Rigid-body violations** — parts of one solid object were animating independently. Regrouped so each rigid object shares one motion: hammer (head+handle now swing together as one tool, instead of the head bending off the handle), the four `arrow-*` icons and `move` (head no longer detaches from shaft/cross — now whole-icon rigid nudges), `undo`/`undo-2`/`redo`/`redo-2` (hook+curve move together), `arrow-right-left` (each arrow's head+line move as one), `plug` (prongs+socket body are one molded piece), `maximize-2`/`minimize-2` (bracket+diagonal shaft are one rigid arm), `box` (shell+seams bounce together, not independently).

**C. Deformations on rigid objects replaced with real rigid motion**: `folder`/`folder-open` no longer skew (shear-deform) — they now use a proper rigid 3D `rotateX` tip; `filter`'s funnel no longer squashes (scaleY) — it settles with a rigid rotate; `cylinder`'s cap lifts (translateY) instead of squashing; `save`'s write-protect tab slides (translateX) instead of hinging into the disk; `landmark`'s columns and `grip-vertical`'s dots no longer slide (which read as the rigid stone/bumps popping loose) — both now use an opacity wave/cascade instead; `hand`'s fingers rotate at their knuckle instead of stretching out of their sockets; `play` depresses (uniform scale, like a real button) instead of growing and sliding; `pipette`'s drop now falls straight down under gravity instead of diagonally; `home`'s door now swings on a vertical-axis `rotateY` hinge through the jamb instead of tipping flat like a trapdoor.

**Bonus catch during verification**: discovered and fixed a real rendering bug in the 3D-rotation technique itself — `perspective()` combined with `rotateX`/`rotateY` explodes to an absurdly oversized rendering when applied to the icon's outer HTML wrapper `<span>` (not a valid `transform-box: view-box` context), but renders correctly at the right proportions when applied to an actual SVG child element (which the shared per-part engine already gives `transform-box: view-box`). Converted folder/folder-open from whole-icon to per-part (targeting their single SVG child) to route through the correct, already-working code path — confirmed by literally measuring the rendered bounding box before (205×190px, exploded) and after (90×90px, correct) via a live browser check. Also retroactively confirmed `home` and `book-open` (which were already per-part) never had this bug.

Verification: full structural validation (154 rules, 0 specificity violations, 0 shared-across-icon animations, 0 dead keyframes, balanced braces, valid postcss parse), all 10 icon tests and the 250-test framework-renderer-react regression suite pass, plus a live interactive visual check — built a self-contained HTML page inlining the real generated icon SVGs and the real ui.css, served over a minimal local HTTP server (the in-session Storybook dev server has a pre-existing streaming issue in this environment's Browser pane unrelated to these changes), froze each animation at its peak keyframe via computed-style-driven negative animation-delay, and visually confirmed: trash-2's lid lifts clear of the bin, lock's shackle pops open, hammer swings as one undivided piece, folder renders at correct size with a subtle 3D tilt, landmark/grip-vertical show a light wave instead of sliding parts.
